title: ATAT: Astronomical Transformer for time series And Tabular data

episodes.description: Build and evaluate ATAT variants and a BHRF baseline on the simulated ELAsTiCC training set; select variants for production.

chain.op: take ELAsTiCC training set (1,845,146 simulated light curves, 32 classes)
discard information absent from alert stream (PHOTFLAG, -30 d window)
Quantile Feature Tokenizer for tabular data
train with Adam and early stopping
compute 429 engineered features and train BHRF baseline
evaluate F1 vs days after first alert, per-class metrics
put two LC+MD+MTA variants into production

notes: All 1430 layout lines (12 pages) read in chunks 1-330, 330-700, 700-1430; pdfinfo 12 pages matches layout page count, all sections present, so the raw .txt was not needed. In L700-1188 purely numeric confusion-matrix cell rows (Fig. 4) were filtered from display; their row/column labels and caption were read. No per-object branches: the paper reports no object-specific human decision. All branches are per_study design choices. No light-curve forecasting of held-out epochs, no model-family choice per object, no cause diagnosis, no follow-up selection is practised. Data are simulations only.
